compiled_state.description:
## Why
rebar's mutating verbs follow the classic Unix rule of silence: `link`, `unlink`, `comment`, `tag`, `edit`, `set-file-impact` exit 0 with empty stdout on success (only `create`/`revert`/`claim` print, because they return generated state). Observed operational cost (2026-08-14, bug clubby-circular-halicore): success, silent idempotent no-op, and swallowed failure are indistinguishable, so agents routinely run a second `rebar show` to verify their own write — an extra store read per mutation — and one agent misread a silent success as a failed write, filed a spurious bug, and retried the identical command (which no-opped silently, compounding the misdiagnosis). Modern CLI practice (clig.dev; kubectl/git/gh/terraform) prints a one-line confirmation of every state change precisely because the caller cannot otherwise see what mutated. rebar's primary operators are agents that must confirm their writes; the confirmation belongs in the mutation's own output.

## Plan
1. Every mutating verb prints ONE line to stdout stating the resulting state, kubectl-style: e.g. `linked <src-alias> -> <target-alias> (<relation>)`, `unlinked ...`, `comment added to <alias> (<n> comments)`, `tagged <alias>: +a +b`, `edited <alias>: description`, `transitioned <alias>: open -> in_progress`. Reuse each command's existing result data — no new store reads to build the message.
2. Idempotent no-ops SAY SO, exit 0 unchanged: `already linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)` (add_dependency's idempotent contract is preserved — the notice is output-only, no event written).
3. `--quiet`/`-q` global flag suppresses the confirmation (scripts); errors unaffected. Where a `--json` output mode exists, confirmations stay off that channel or ride a structured field — never corrupt JSON output.
4. Confirmation goes to STDOUT (it is the command's result, not a diagnostic); warnings/logs stay on stderr. Exit codes remain the programmatic contract, unchanged.
5. Inventory pass: enumerate mutating CLI verbs (transition/link/unlink/comment/tag/edit/claim/reopen/set-file-impact/session-log/tracker-maintenance...), apply the pattern uniformly; verbs that already print (create, revert, claim) keep their output, normalized to the same style. MCP tools are OUT OF SCOPE (their outputSchemas already return structured results).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each mutating CLI verb prints a one-line stdout confirmation naming the operation and resulting state; per-verb tests assert the line and that no extra store read is performed to build it.
- [ ] Idempotent no-op paths (at minimum: re-link of an identical active edge) print an explicit already-X notice, still exit 0, still write no event (store-event count asserted).
- [ ] --quiet suppresses confirmations; JSON output modes remain valid JSON (tested).
- [ ] Confirmations on stdout, logs/warnings on stderr (tested via captured streams); no exit-code changes (existing exit-code contract tests stay green).
- [ ] docs/user-guide.md + cli-reference regenerated; `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
compiled_state.title: Mutating CLI verbs confirm their result on stdout (kubectl-style; already-X notices for idempotent no-ops)
